claim: Human attentional capture is contingent on the control setting in the classic cueing designs: cues that match the searched-for feature capture, others mostly do not (Folk 1992, Folk and Remington 1998, Eimer and Kiss 2008, Folk et al. 2008 in time). A meta-analysis of 64 experiments agrees, with moderators (target a singleton, blocked vs mixed).
agent_test: Plant a vivid irrelevant item in a task whose goal is stated first vs stated last; the item matching the goal should pull more than a mismatched one.

claim: Without an active control setting, salient items produce a priority signal and capture. All three rival camps (contingent, stimulus-driven, signal-suppression) now agree on this and on the fact that control can prevent capture.
agent_test: Compare planted-hint vs no-hint accuracy with no goal statement; then with the goal stated before the material.

claim: Whether top-down control can beat very high salience is still contested: Wang and Theeuwes (2020) found suppression at set size 4 but not 6 or 10; Stilwell and Gaspelin found suppression at 10 and 30 items and call the set-size result a floor effect.
agent_test: Not directly testable on an LLM; it is a human-mechanism dispute. Use as a warning not to claim a stated goal always blocks a strong plant.

claim: Suppression of a distractor feature needs a predictable feature and builds with experience: with a random colour the suppression vanished (Gaspelin and Luck 2018, N=24 and 28), and learned rejection appears after 2 or 3 encounters (Savelson 2025, after a failed split-block replication).
agent_test: Vary whether the planted distractor type is the same across items in a run; test if a one-line lesson about its type (S9) cuts its pull on later items.

claim: Learned location regularities reduce capture, even in feature search, while telling people the location trial by trial did not (Wang and Theeuwes 2018a,b).
agent_test: Only one lab reports it. Test whether a stored class-level note (hints in this class are wrong x% of the time) beats a per-item instruction to ignore.

claim: Reward history and selection history are a third source of capture beside goals and salience (Anderson 2011: 16, 15, 16 ms after 4 to 21 days; Failing 2015: 7.8% vs 3.1% and 19.6% vs 7.4% first saccades). Effects are small and the paradigm has confounds and weak, mixed reliability.
agent_test: In a long run, check whether an item type that paid off earlier gets over-weighted later; compare with history shown vs stripped.

claim: Capture is brief in time: a salient item's pull is gone by about 150 ms, so reaction-time cueing designs can hide it. Only direct measures (detection d', eye movements, ERP) show it. Sources come mostly from one lab.
agent_test: Not testable in text. Measurement lesson only: a final-answer check can hide that a plant was read and then discarded; compare first-draft and final-answer deviation.

claim: Group-level distractor effects are robust but individual-level suppression scores are unreliable (Ivanov 2024); ADHD adults showed similar capture but slower disengagement (Zhang 2024).
agent_test: No direct agent test. Use only to avoid per-item claims about how one model attends.

claim: Adding one irrelevant sentence to a math problem cuts LLM accuracy. GSM-IC: no more than 18% of base problems solved under all distractor types; CoT micro 72.4 vs macro 6.0 (code-davinci-002). GSM-NoOp: drops up to 65%, larger for newer models. CatAttack: appended triggers raise error rates in reasoning models (by multiples of the random-chance rate, see critique). Gap search (2025-2026): the drop persists in reasoning models. Opus 4 ~100% to 85-90% and R1 70% to 30% with 5 planted puzzles; o3 97.4 to 93.9 with many number-bearing clauses; GPT-4.1 step accuracy 26% to 2% at 15 distractors; Gemini-2.5-Pro lost 38% on NoisyBench. Reasoning mode shrinks but does not remove it (small models: 41 down to 14-20 points). No 2026 test of GSM-NoOp or CatAttack on current frontier models was found.
agent_test: Build a 100-item set with one planted irrelevant clause; measure accuracy of plain vs S1 input hygiene at equal tokens, on the current model (evidence is 2022 to 2025 era).

claim: Distractors that look relevant (same role, same topic, semantically related) hurt more than unrelated ones, and more distractors hurt more. GSM-IC: role overlap drove text-davinci-003 macro accuracy to 0 on problems over 2 steps. COL-Bench: related passages mislead far more. GSM-DC: error rises as a power law in distractor count. Gap search: relevance-gated pull seen again (relevant false passage costs 0.12-0.43, irrelevant at most 0.06; NoisyBench similarity raises tokens and lowers accuracy). Same-template distractors beat same-topic ones (Claude Sonnet 4 0.889, GPT-4.1 0.967 vs 1.000 for topical and unrelated).
agent_test: Plant three types (random, in-topic, role-overlap) and vary the count; S1 hygiene should help most on role-overlap.

claim: An instruction to ignore irrelevant material helps a little but does not remove the pull (GSM-IC instruction gain; S2A instructed prompting 62.8 to 71.7 vs rewrite 80.3; Wu 2024 ignore instruction limited; anchoring prompt mitigation insufficient). Gap search: NoisyBench prompting and context engineering did not help; a one-sentence unreliability warning did (+0.18 voting, 8 of 9 cells) while a verifier agent did not. Code-side stripping has still not been tested.
agent_test: Arm A plain, arm B an ignore-irrelevant line, arm C code-side stripping of suggestive content; same tokens.

claim: Rewriting the context to keep only relevant parts before answering (System 2 Attention) beat instructed ignoring: factual QA 62.8 to 80.3 (oracle 82.0); GSM-IC in-topic 51.7 to 61.3. One model family (LLaMA-2-70B-chat), one paper.
agent_test: Replicate on the current model: S1 restate step with the original beside it vs an S2A-style rewrite; check for dropped needed facts.

claim: Self-consistency (20 samples) lifts GSM-IC micro accuracy by over 11 points (35.5 for 0-shot CoT), but best macro accuracy stays 45%, and the correct answer is among the 20 samples for 99.7% of problems. Same-model samples share the same pull.
agent_test: Harvest candidates by code (S4) and test them on a fresh input; compare with plain majority vote on the planted set.

claim: Planted hints (suggested answer, always-A) shift LLM answers strongly and the chain of thought almost never names them. Turpin 2023: suggested answer -36.3 (GPT-3.5 zero-shot), -30.6 (Claude 1.0); bias mentioned in 0 of 234 sampled. Chen 2025: reasoning models verbalise hint use rarely, average 25% (Claude 3.7 Sonnet) and 39% (R1).
agent_test: Plant a hint and check whether the written reasoning names it; decide from outputs, not text (G10). Count how often a hint changes the answer per class.

claim: User-stated beliefs and challenges pull assistants: a wrong suggested answer cuts accuracy up to 27% (LLaMA 2); Claude 1.3 wrongly admits mistakes on 98% of challenged questions; a preference model prefers sycophantic replies about 45% of the time on the hardest misconceptions; scale and instruction tuning raise repeating the user's opinion (Wei 2023).
agent_test: Add a user-stated wrong belief to items; S1 moves it out of the model's view vs left in. Also test G2: revision only from real output, not from an are-you-sure challenge.

claim: Numeric or expert anchor hints shift LLM estimates, and prompt-level mitigation (CoT, ignore, reflection) is not sufficient; reasoning models show the lowest anchoring ratios in one benchmark. Evidence is thin (62 questions, student authors, small models).
agent_test: Run an anchor set with and without code-side stripping of the numeric hint; compare to reasoning-on.

claim: Position matters: accuracy is U-shaped over where the relevant passage sits (GPT-3.5-Turbo 56.1% closed-book, 88.3% oracle; the middle position can fall below closed-book). It tests use of relevant information, not capture by a plant. Gap search: question-first (before distractor-laden documents) lost 18.3 and 25.0 needle points and 10.7 LongBench points in small models; Anthropic advises queries last (up to 30%).
agent_test: Place the key fact at start, middle, end of context; test whether S1 restate-at-top removes the dip on current models.

claim: Multimodal LLMs show partial pop-out analogues: flat cost for single-feature search, rising cost for conjunction (GPT-4o 83% flat on the large-circle task; reasoning tokens per item at most 0.5 for feature vs 2.76 to 4.98 for conjunction). Claude and Llama are weaker. Tests target search, not capture by a distractor.
agent_test: Not for schema decisions; a lens only: salience-like effects exist in vision-language models.

claim: Reasoning models with adaptive thinking decline to deliberate on tasks they judge easy; this removes a chance to filter a planted item (author caveat, one preprint). Gap search: the Wick result is about visual search, not planted-easy items; no study tests a restate gate. Still open.
agent_test: Test whether a gate that forces a short restate step (S1) fixes failures on planted-easy items for an adaptive-thinking model.

claim: Distractor-rich training helps (GSM-DC hard-distractor fine-tune: 77.95 in-domain step accuracy vs 35.91 clean), but it does not transfer to a scaffold-only agent. Process-reward beam search gave +2.69 to +6.29 out-of-domain.
agent_test: Not testable without training. Skip.

claim: Free-form answers resist irrelevant inputs better than multiple choice (Llama2-7B misrepresentation 14.1 free-form vs 42.4 multiple choice at 3:1). Multiple-choice options make the lure explicit.
agent_test: On an open-answer item, ask for a free-form answer before showing options; compare.

claim: Theory moved from a two-way split toward one priority map with three inputs (goals, salience, selection history), and some argue the question was it captured is the wrong binary (Awh 2012, Anderson 2021, Luck 2021 common framework, Guided Search 6.0).
agent_test: Design lesson: treat pull as a continuous weight with proactive (before input) and reactive (after first pass) control.

claim: Singleton-detection mode (the capture-prone mode) was judged more effortful than feature-search mode, against the earlier assumption (Lee, Clement, Anderson 2023, Exp 1 N=40).
agent_test: No agent test.

claim: Putting the question or goal before distractor-laden material does not protect and can hurt: in three 3-4B models question-first cost 18.3 and 25.0 needle points (always returning a distractor's value) and 10.7 LongBench points; a generic task description first was fine (+4.3 LongBench). Anthropic advises the query last (up to 30%). No test exists of goal-before versus goal-after with a planted hint in a 2026 reasoning model.
agent_test: Plant one hint; compare goal-before, goal-after and both, at equal tokens, on the current model.

claim: LLM pull is gated by relevance and by structure, as contingent capture would predict, but no study separates match from salience cleanly. On-topic false passages cost 0.12-0.43 accuracy vs at most 0.06 off-topic (open models); same-template distractors beat same-topic ones for Claude Sonnet 4 and GPT-4.1; NoisyBench similarity raises error. None tests wording overlap with a stated goal.
agent_test: Plant items that match the stated goal's role words, match the template only, or neither; hold position and length fixed.

claim: Typographic salience is weak at the frontier. All-caps framing had no effect on judgments in Gemini-3.1, Gemini-2.5, Claude Opus 4.6 and GPT-5.4-pro (effect size unreported); casing draws more attention in non-reasoning models but accuracy does not follow, and thinking appears to buffer it. Position (question-first) and format-copying matter more.
agent_test: Bold, capitalise, repeat and move a hint to the top or end, with wording fixed.

claim: Extra thinking does not undo a planted distraction: Claude Opus 4 and DeepSeek R1 get worse with longer reasoning on simple counting with planted puzzles, and traces show the model considers the simple answer and then returns to the distractor. So there is no sign of human-like fast capture followed by recovery. Measure at the final answer, and log the draft.
agent_test: Record the first-draft answer and the final answer on planted items.

claim: Distraction and sycophancy are separable. Four frontier models (Gemini-3.1-pro, Gemini-2.5-pro, Claude Opus 4.6, GPT-5.4-pro) left their judgments unmoved by an irrelevant turn but GPT and Gemini shifted 2-6.5% toward the user's stated view (Claude was not significantly steered). Sycophantic commitment builds during the chain. One S1 hygiene step does not obviously cover both: use a content filter and a separate rule against adopting stated beliefs.
agent_test: Run planted clause, planted user belief and planted anchor on the same items; check whether one fix moves all three.

claim: Class-level and model-side fixes: a one-sentence warning that supplied information may be unreliable recovered up to +0.18 (voting) in 8 of 9 cells at no cost when context was true; a verifier agent added nothing; prompting and context-engineering tools failed on NoisyBench. This is an unplanned partial test of a class-level lesson; the stored-lesson versus per-item instruction comparison and code-side stripping remain untested.
agent_test: Compare code-side removal, S2A rewrite, an ignore sentence and a stored class note at equal tokens.

claim: Earlier conversation state persists and a recap only partly clears it: models lost 39% in multi-turn use because early assumptions were over-relied upon, and repeating information each turn mitigated 15-20% of the loss. Agents under noise carried distractor-shaped hypotheses across planning steps. Supports fresh contexts indirectly; selection history by item type has not been tested in LLMs.
agent_test: Run items after a block of rewarded planted-style items, with and without a fresh context.
